findings: HMB seawater streams 25/26 (10,196.8 kg/s in all cases) equal 36,050 m3/h at about 1,018 kg/m3 (IG-04) and give 7 K rise, but the CW system, pumps and intake are sized for 38,000 m3/h per DEC-EPCE-0002; CW pumps rated 2 x 19,000 m3/h. AL-12 power at 38,000 m3/h and 16 m would be about 2.04 MW instead of 1.94 MW.

CW pump rated_power 1,900 kW was the total of both pumps (AL-12 = 1.94 MW for 2 x 50 %), not per pump; corrected to 1,120 kW per pump (MV 10 kV); the equipment list would otherwise double the CW power (3.8 MW installed).

CW pump head 16 m in AL-12 is a bare value; condenser + tube-side + pipe + outfall head loss must be confirmed (rated 17 m, +6 %). Condenser inlet stream 25 is 2.5 bar(a) and outlet 1.7 bar(a), i.e. 0.8 bar across the condenser alone.

AL-14 electro-chlorination 260 kW covers only about 45 kg/h Cl2 at 5 kWh/kg (1.2 ppm on 38,000 m3/h); sized for 1.5 ppm (60 kg/h) the package draws about 340 kW. Owner limit for residual chlorine at the outfall is 0.1 mg/l (DP-CASE-0017), so dosing 1.5 ppm requires seawater chlorine demand above 1.4 mg/l or a dechlorination / reduced dose strategy; Black Sea salinity 22-26 PSU (chloride up to 14,500 mg/l, DP-OWNR-0014) also lowers cell efficiency. Chlorination booster pump 37 kW is oversized (15 kW).

AL-13 CCW pumps 320 kW is twice the 160 kW motor of one pump although the arrangement is 2 x 100 % (1 running): expected electrical load about 150 kW; either AL-13 is conservative or two pumps are assumed running (raise as an assumption, effect about 0.03 % on net heat rate).

AL-10 BFP and AL-11 CEP have no power input (pump_node method from enthalpy rise) and no pump efficiency; existing BFP rating 3,600 kW was not an IEC size (now 4,000 kW) and CEP 450 kW was oversized (now 355 kW). The 'feedwater to BFP' stream 21 equals streams 22 + 23 in SRC-NG-100 but sprays (29/30) add on top in SUM/MAX cases only: BFP sized on the maximum total 134.9 kg/s (WIN-NG-100).

HMB streams: WIN-NG-100 (cold winter) is the sizing case for BFP/CEP flow (134.9 / 133.9 kg/s), with MIN-NG-100 second; the maximum flow occurs at low seawater temperature, when condenser pressure is lowest (CEP suction 0.022 bar(a), full-vacuum NPSH design required).

Condensate polishing (00LDA) is 2 vessels 2 x 100 %: no third vessel or external regeneration vessel is listed in the equipment data; confirm concept (service/standby with external regeneration) and resin-limit 60 degC. Polisher is listed at full condensate flow 530 t/h.

Electro-chlorination package: no dechlorination/sodium bisulfite dosing, no hypochlorite tank level/transfer pumps and no CW intake dosing manifold are listed; storage sized only as a buffer (2.5 h). No CCW make-up pumps, no CW pump priming / ball-collector items listed either.

CCW cooler duty 10 MW is an estimate from aux_load AL-01..04 and generator loss assumptions; no consumer list exists in the database. Seawater supply for the CCW plate exchangers (about 1,100 m3/h) is not shown by any equipment or HMB stream and must be taken from the CW system.
CW ball recirculation pumps/debris filters are listed as 2 x 100 % / A-B; adopted 2 x 50 % (one per condenser half) - confirm with the cleaning-system supplier.

Ammonia system: estimated consumption 0.27 m3/h of 25 % aqueous ammonia from NOx 25 to 3 ppm; existing 4 kW forwarding pump is oversized (1.1 kW). No ammonia vaporiser/dilution air blower listed in 10HSB (probably part of SCR package).
